best_for: Developers who know the HTTPie command line and want the same plain approach in a desktop API client, without signing up for anything to start.

points.title: Works without an account
points.text: Without signing in, the app runs in an incognito mode that keeps everything in local storage. Sign in later and that local data moves into your account.

points.title: What an account adds
points.text: An account gives unlimited spaces, cloud backup, live sync across devices and the AI assistant, which the docs say is free with an account while it is in preview. Without one you cannot sync or create new spaces.

points.title: Offline first
points.text: Requests, collections and environments keep working with no connection, and syncing resumes once you are back online. Environments can be marked local-only so their values never leave the device.

points.title: Free, but not open source
points.text: The desktop app is closed-source freeware under HTTPie's own terms. The GitHub repository holds releases and the issue tracker, not the source code. The separate HTTPie command-line tool is a different product.

points.title: Linux route
points.text: HTTPie publishes an AppImage and recommends AppImageLauncher to run it. The Flatpak listed here comes from Flathub, which does not mark it as verified by HTTPie.

points.title: Slow release pace
points.text: The newest desktop release is 2025.2.0. The Windows listing keeps 10 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release. The Windows installer can install per user or for all users.
